name: Magnetic soft wire
full_name: MIT telerobotic magnetic soft guidewire system
group: Zhao lab, MIT, with Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School (neurosurgery), University of Cincinnati and Philips Research North America; animal work under UMass Medical School IACUC (kim2022_telerobotic affiliations, p. 18)
versions: 2019 ferromagnetic soft continuum robots: device only, magnet moved by hand and wire pushed by hand (kim2019_ferromagnetic); 2022 telerobotic system: KUKA arm with a 100 mm magnet, two motorised advancers, remote console, 400 um wire, pig (kim2022_telerobotic)
target_anatomy: neuro (phantoms, porcine brachial artery with accentuated tortuosity)
devices_driven: 2 devices, driven independently or simultaneously: own magnetic soft guidewire, 400 um OD (tapered nitinol core in a TPU jacket with 20 vol% NdFeB, magnetically responsive distal 50 mm, coreless 4 mm tip) and a microcatheter; 0.0115-in coils and a Solitaire X stent retriever delivered through it; 7 F sheath (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3-4, 18); 2019 prototypes 600 um (PDMS + NdFeB, 80 um nitinol core) and 810 um (TPU + NdFeB) (kim2019_ferromagnetic)
n_dof_detail: 7-DOF arm (KUKA LBR Med 14 R820) sets the magnet pose (6-DOF end-effector control; pole flipped by turning axis 7 by 180 degrees) + 2 linear advancing units for wire and microcatheter (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3, 7, 17)
translation_detail: magnetic (steering); insertion by two commercial worm-drive advancers (Stereotaxis QuikCAS Cardiodrive) driven by DC gearmotors through flexible shafts (kim2022_telerobotic p. 3, 18)
device_range: magnet working distance d/R 2.64-3.67, i.e. 80-30 mT at the tip (kim2022_telerobotic p. 7)
footprint_mm: N.R. (arm on a mobile platform beside the operating table, kim2022_telerobotic p. 3)
mass_kg: magnet and fixture 7 kg (kim2022_telerobotic p. 18); arm N.R.
force_sensing: none: 'the advancing unit of our system does not provide any tactile or haptic feedback' (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17)
haptics_leader: no haptics: remote console a few metres away with a 6-DOF SpaceMouse Pro knob and buttons to advance/retract; ROS MoveIt/RViz virtual view (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17-18)
imaging_compat: real-time fluoroscopy, DSA roadmaps, 3D rotational angiography; the NdFeB particles make the wire radiopaque; compatible with standard biplane fluoroscopy (kim2022_telerobotic p. 8, 17)
validation_detail: head phantom under fluoroscopy (navigation 45.0 +- 4.0 s, n = 5); MCA aneurysm coiling and clot retrieval in phantoms (n = 3 each); 1 pig (56 kg Yorkshire, brachial-artery tortuosity model, 124.6 +- 19.7 s, n = 5); learning curve 6 novices and 2 experienced users x 15 trials; robot vs manual: one interventionalist, 10 trials each (kim2022_telerobotic pp. 8-16, 18)
key_numbers: robot vs manual 42.9 +- 10.5 vs 63.7 +- 22.4 s (P < 0.05); the manual wire crossed the siphon aneurysm in 5 of 10 trials; field at most 80 mT, gradient 1.75 mT/mm; N52 cylindrical magnet 100 mm diameter x 100 mm; tip deflection about 120 deg (attraction) and 90 deg (repulsion) (kim2022_telerobotic pp. 5-16)
sim_model: field maps in COMSOL; 2019 Abaqus finite-element model of the soft continuum robot (kim2019_ferromagnetic p. 13); MoveIt/RViz virtual scene used to plan magnet poses; magnet pose from joystick input via a Jacobian pseudo-inverse, no guidewire model in the loop (kim2022_telerobotic p. 17)
sim2real_detail: none found (no learned controller in kim2019 or kim2022)
